questions.question: Which theme asks where a place is located?
Which theme describes the physical and human characteristics of a location?
Which theme examines how people adapt to and change their surroundings?
Which theme examines flows of people, goods, and ideas?
Which theme groups places by shared characteristics?
What is absolute location?
choices: A description using nearby landmarks only
A grouping of places by language
A precise position such as coordinates
A pattern of goods moving between cities

questions.question: What is relative location?
choices: A position expressed only by exact coordinates
A position described in relation to other places
A region with a shared climate

questions.question: Why are latitude and longitude useful for location?
choices: They describe every cultural feature of a place
They reveal every movement of goods
They classify all regions by language
They identify precise positions on Earth's surface

questions.question: Why do climate and architecture both belong to the theme of place?
choices: Place includes physical and human characteristics

questions.question: How does a dam illustrate human-environment interaction?
choices: It provides a city's exact coordinates
People modify a river to serve human purposes
It identifies a region solely by shared voting patterns

questions.question: Why does migration fit the theme of movement?
choices: Migration describes rainfall without human activity

questions.question: What makes a language region a formal region?
choices: It is defined only by travel time to one central point
It must have legally identical political boundaries
It consists only of individual opinions about a place
It is defined by a shared measurable characteristic

questions.question: What makes a metropolitan commuting area a functional region?
choices: Activities connect surrounding places to a central city
Every place within it has the same climate
It is defined only by a shared continent

questions.question: Why can a perceptual region have disputed boundaries?
choices: Its coordinates are always fixed by international treaty
It depends on people's ideas and impressions of an area
It is defined only by a river drainage basin

questions.question: Why can the five themes overlap in a geographic study?
choices: Each theme must be studied without reference to others
One issue can involve location, characteristics, interactions, flows, and regions
Every place has only one geographic characteristic

questions.question: A student describes a town as 20 miles east of another town. Which concept is used?
A map gives a school's latitude and longitude. Which concept is used?
A farmer uses terraces to grow crops on slopes. Which theme is most directly illustrated?
A researcher tracks clothing shipped from factories to stores overseas. Which theme is central?
Which study most directly applies the theme of region?
choices: Finding one house by street address
Describing a single farmer's irrigation choice
Comparing areas that share a Mediterranean climate
